quotes.text: Low code changes how you build. It does not remove the need to manage change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compresses the episode's argument that low-code still needs lifecycle discipline.

quotes.text: Managed environments add order around the container, but CICD controls movement through the container. Those are different jobs. One helps govern the space, the other governs change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates what Managed Environments do from what CI/CD does.

quotes.text: Most teams govern access first. The stronger teams govern change first because that's where operational risk actually shows up.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise, actionable reframing of governance priorities.

quotes.text: If your app lifecycle is shaky, AI is just going to scale that shakiness. If your integration layer is brittle, AI is going to lean on it until it snaps.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why AI and Copilot amplify weak delivery foundations.

quotes.text: Managed environments don't fail because the idea of governance is wrong. They fail because governance was asked to do the job of engineering and release control and it simply can't do those things.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the root cause named in the episode title.

chapters.title: Why Managed Environments promise control but stall delivery
The ghost town effect of locked governance
The hidden wall between low-code and pro-code
Why delivery fails without embedded CI/CD
How integration debt turns managed platforms into liabilities
Why AI and Copilot make the gap impossible to ignore
The model that works: governance with a pro-dev spine

takeaways: Managed Environments govern access, monitoring and policy, but they do not replace source control, build validation, release approvals or rollback paths.
Enterprise Power Platform apps need ALM through CI/CD, for example with Azure DevOps, plus a governed integration layer with clear endpoint ownership instead of scattered connector logic.
Zone workloads into maker-led, fusion and pro-dev tiers and measure release frequency, failed deployments and orphaned apps instead of inventory counts, especially before scaling AI and Copilot.
hook: Managed Environments were supposed to bring order to the Power Platform, yet many organizations see critical apps stall and pro developers walk away. This episode is for Power Platform admins, architects and IT leaders who pay for governance but struggle to ship. Learn why governance needs a pro-dev spine with ALM, CI/CD and disciplined integration to deliver safely.
